title: National Sports Tribunal Bill 2019
portfolio: Regional Services, Sport, Local Government and Decentralisation

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill is part of a two-bill package that would create the National Sports Tribunal to resolve sporting disputes.
The tribunal would handle cases through private arbitration, mediation, conciliation or case appraisal, and its jurisdiction would depend on agreements between the parties.
The bill sets a two-year time limit for making applications, unless the rules specify a longer period.
changes: Establishes the National Sports Tribunal with several divisions, including an anti-doping division.
Allows for the appointment of tribunal members and a chief executive officer.
Sets out processes for applying to the tribunal for arbitration or alternative dispute resolution.
Gives the minister power to make rules by legislative instrument.
Imposes a two-year time limit on applications, extendable by rules.
Makes consequential amendments to the Australian Sports Anti-Doping Authority Act 2006.
summary.affected: The Australian sporting community, including athletes, sports organisations and anti-doping authorities.

speeches.speaker: Greg Hunt
speeches.brief: The National Sports Tribunal (Consequential Amendments and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2019 was introduced as a companion to the National Sports Tribunal Bill 2019, covering transitional arrangements and transferring sports dispute resolution functions to the new tribunal. It amends the Australian Sports Anti-Doping Authority Act 2006, with the changes taking effect before the tribunal's establishment on 1 July 2019.
